title: Ecogeographical rules & the island rule
sub: Lectures 2 & 3 · Bergmann, Allen, Gloger, island rule, meta-analysis
blurb: Body size and colour along climate gradients, giants and dwarfs on islands, how to read a paper.
h1: Patterns in body size, shape and colour
lede: The end of Lecture 2 (ecogeographical rules) and the Lecture 3 example talk on the island rule, plus how a scientific paper is built. Glossary section 6 i–l.
six: **Bergmann's rule**: larger bodies in colder climates.
**Allen's rule**: shorter extremities in cold regions.
**Gloger's rule**: darker pigmentation in warm, humid areas.
**Island rule** (Foster's rule): small species get bigger (**gigantism**), large species get smaller (**dwarfism**) on islands.

A **meta-analysis** statistically combines results of many studies; for the island rule, author groups disagree, so the verdict is: it generally holds, but depends on context and lineage, and methods matter.
Abstract → Introduction (what is known), Methods (data & stats), Results, Discussion (interpretation).

questions.q: Which rule says animals in colder climates tend to have larger bodies?
questions.e: Bergmann: larger bodies in colder climates.

questions.q: Which rule says animals in cold regions have shorter extremities (ears, legs)?
questions.e: Allen: shorter extremities in cold regions.

questions.q: Which rule links darker pigmentation to warm, humid areas?
questions.e: Gloger: darker colour in warm, humid areas.

questions.q: What does the island rule predict?
questions.answer: Small species get bigger and large species get smaller on islands
wrong: All species get smaller on islands
All species get bigger on islands

questions.q: Large animals evolving a smaller body size on islands is called…
questions.e: Linked to limited resources and relaxed predation.

questions.q: Why might small animals get bigger on islands (insular gigantism)?
questions.answer: Less predation and competition open new opportunities
wrong: More food than on the mainland
questions.e: Glossary 6k: presumably reduced predation and competition.

questions.q: Which two factors does the glossary link to insular dwarfism?
questions.e: Smaller, more resource-efficient individuals are favoured.

questions.q: The island rule is also called…
questions.e: After Bristol Foster; Leigh Van Valen is also linked to it.

questions.answer: A statistical synthesis that combines effect sizes from many independent studies
wrong: A review that lists papers without statistics
A model of a single population
questions.e: Used to estimate overall patterns and test how robust a hypothesis is.

questions.q: What was the Lecture 3 synthesis on the island rule?
questions.answer: It generally holds, but depends on context and lineage, and methods matter
questions.e: Lokatis & Jeschke 2018 show author groups disagree; phylogenetic vs non-phylogenetic models give different answers.

questions.q: In a paper, 'what is known' from the abstract is expanded in which section?
questions.e: Abstract parts map to Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion.

questions.q: Where do the authors interpret their results?
How was song complexity measured in the Lecture 3 songbird study?
questions.answer: Number of different note types in a sequence of 50 notes
wrong: Length of the song in seconds
questions.e: About 18,500 recordings of 4,940 species were screened manually.

questions.q: What explains extreme song complexity, according to that talk?
questions.answer: Vocal learning, ecological context and evolutionary history together
